In conclusion, 8 is a small, easily labeled, and highly stable prosthetic group with promising potential for developing stable radioiodinated drugs and broadening their therapeutic application.

item.title: Discovery of Neurolysin Activators with Preclinical Efficacy in an Ischemic Stroke Model
item.description:
Abstract
The peptidase neurolysin (Nln) is upregulated following ischemic stroke to activate endogenous cerebroprotective mechanisms and has subsequently emerged as a therapeutic target for drug discovery efforts. Overexpression of Nln in a mouse model of ischemic stroke results in significant improvement of stroke outcomes. Herein, we report the discovery of the first non-peptide Nln activators based around a central pyridine-piperazine scaffold that possesses nanomolar potency. This scaffold, exemplified by compounds 7c and 7g, exhibits greater in vitro half-life, blood−brain barrier penetration, mouse brain and mouse plasma stability than previously reported peptidomimetic Nln activators. Compound 7g afforded an in vivo protective effect in the MCAO mouse model of ischemic stroke, significantly reducing infarct volume and brain water content, marking the first report of a small molecule Nln activator with in vivo cerebroprotective effects in a preclinical model.

item.title: Discovery and Optimization of Indole-Based CDK9 Inhibitors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma
item.description:
Abstract
CDK9 has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for anticancer drug development. Although multiple CDK9 inhibitors have entered clinical evaluation, differentiated scaffolds with convincing activity and tolerability in solid tumors remain limited. In this study, we identified a series of indole-based CDK9 inhibitors through virtual screening and structure-based drug design, and systematically evaluated their therapeutic potential in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Among these compounds, W24 exhibited potent CDK9 inhibitory activity (IC50 = 0.9 nM) and a preliminary kinase selectivity profile. W24 effectively induced HCC cell death in vitro, which was accompanied by DNA damage and downregulation of the anti-apoptotic protein Mcl-1. Furthermore, W24 significantly suppressed tumor growth in HepG2 and Huh-7 xenograft models with an acceptable safety profile under the tested dosing regimen. Collectively, these findings highlight W24 as a promising lead compound and provide valuable insights for the development of next-generation CDK9 inhibitors for the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma.

item.title: Lung-Tailored Pyrrolo-pyrimidine DDR Inhibitors Designed for Optimized Local Delivery
item.description:
Abstract
Preclinical studies highlighted the key role of Discoidin Domain Receptors (DDRs) in fibrotic processes, making them promising targets for Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) treatment. In this work, we describe the design of a novel class of DDR inhibitors and their subsequent optimization toward inhaled delivery. Following a structure-based approach, we identified two chemical series based on 5:6 heterocyclic cores showing nanomolar affinity for DDR1 and DDR2 and a promising kinome selectivity profile. An inhaled-by-design medchem strategy was then applied to optimize potency, phys-chem, and in vitro ADME properties, tailored to achieve lung-restricted compounds. This effort resulted in the discovery of compound 25, a novel and highly potent DDR inhibitor that combined antifibrotic activity in a TGFβ-induced in vitro fibrosis model with an outstanding pharmacokinetic profile and the desired lung-targeted behavior following inhaled administration.

item.title: Design and Biological Evaluation of FAP-Man, a Mannosylated FAP-Targeted Radioglycopeptide for Tumor Imaging and Radionuclide Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is an attractive target for radiotheranostic development because of its abundant expression in tumor-associated fibroblasts and limited distribution in normal tissues. Here, we developed FAP-Man, a mannosylated FAP-targeted radioglycopeptide based on the FAP-2286 scaffold, to optimize tumor targeting and pharmacokinetic properties. Compared with [68Ga]Ga-FAP-2286, [68Ga]Ga-FAP-Man showed higher tumor uptake in U87MG tumor-bearing mice (16.917 ± 4.986 vs 3.188 ± 0.535 %ID/g at 1 h post-injection) and improved tumor-to-liver contrast. Both [177Lu]Lu-FAP-Man and [225Ac]Ac-FAP-Man significantly inhibited tumor growth compared with PBS-treated controls. Preliminary clinical PET imaging further supported its potential for favorable lesion visualization and lesion-to-background contrast, particularly for hepatic lesions. These findings support further evaluation of FAP-Man as a FAP-targeted radiopharmaceutical candidate.

item.title: Influence of Fluorine Substitution Pattern in Arylboronic Acid Caps on the Myocardial Perfusion Imaging Properties of Technetium Monocapped Tris(dioxime) Complexes
item.description:
Abstract
Boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers represent a promising scaffold for quantitative SPECT myocardial blood flow (MBF) imaging. In this study, five fluorinated 99mTc-labeled boronate derivatives were designed to systematically investigate the influence of fluorine substitution patterns on tracer pharmacokinetics and imaging performance. The fluorination pattern markedly influenced myocardial uptake, hepatic clearance, and overall biodistribution, with 99mTc-2F-HMPBA (99mTc-2F) and 99mTc-3F-HMPBA (99mTc-3F) exhibiting the most favorable profiles. Mechanistic evaluation using isolated heart perfusion demonstrated a high first-pass extraction fraction over a wide range of coronary flow rates, while dynamic SPECT imaging in swine showed tracer-derived K1 values comparable to 13N−NH3 PET-derived MBF. In particular, 99mTc-3F exhibited a more balanced pharmacokinetic profile with improved heart-to-liver contrast. These findings establish fluorine substitution as an effective strategy for tuning the pharmacokinetic behavior of boronate-based myocardial perfusion tracers and identify 99mTc-3F as a promising lead for quantitative SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging.

item.title: Modular Biomimetic Strategy toward Discovery of Macrocyclic Sulfonamides as SIRT3 Activators against Heart Failure
item.description:
Abstract
Heart failure (HF) remains a severe global cardiovascular disease with limited targeted therapies. Mitochondrial deacetylase SIRT3 is a promising therapeutic target for HF, yet current SIRT3 agonists suffer from low potency and poor isoform selectivity. Herein, we adopted a modular biomimetic strategy to synthesize a series of macrocyclic sulfonamides and systematically explored their structure-activity relationships. The lead compound 2b (Y0855) exhibited potent SIRT3 agonistic activity (EC50 = 12.6 μM, and Emax = 4.05) and excellent selectivity over SIRT1/2/6. Mechanistically, 2b alleviated cardiomyocyte oxidative stress, cell injury and fibrosis via SIRT3 activation. In a doxorubicin-induced HF mouse model, it markedly restored cardiac function and mitigated myocardial damage. Moreover, 2b possessed improved metabolic stability, making it a valuable lead compound for anti-HF drug development targeting SIRT3.

item.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Janus Kinase (JAK) and Histone Deacetylase (HDAC) Dual Inhibitors for the Treatment of Psoriasis
item.description:
Abstract
Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory dermatosis featured by aberrant keratinocyte hyperproliferation and persistent cutaneous inflammatory infiltration, lacking curative small-molecule therapeutics. Dysregulated Janus kinase signal transducer and activator of transcription pathway (JAK/STAT) and histone deacetylase (HDAC)-dependent epigenetic signaling represented essential pathogenic axes driving psoriasis progression. Inspired by synergistic crosstalk between these two pathways and our previous work identifying anti-psoriatic JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors, a series of novel dual JAK/HDAC inhibitors were rationally designed and synthesized. Systematic enzymatic profiling revealed compound 11e exerted potent and balanced JAK2 and HDAC6 inhibitory activity (JAK2 IC50 = 2.1 nM, HDAC6 IC50 = 3.1 nM). Critically, topical cream formulation and oral administration of 11e dramatically alleviated erythema, scaling, and epidermal hyperplasia in the imiquimod-induced psoriasis mouse model. Collectively, compound 11e served as a promising lead compound for anti-psoriasis drug development, providing validated structural scaffolds for further optimization of next-generation JAK/HDAC dual inhibitors.

item.title: Alkyl-Branched Acyl-Lysine Peptides as Potent Cell-Permeable Slow-Substrate Inhibitors of SIRT2
item.description:
Abstract
Sirtuin 2 (SIRT2) is a nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+)-dependent lysine deacylase implicated in cancer and neurodegeneration. Here, we report acyl-lysine peptide inhibitors bearing methyl-branched or cyclopropyl-modified acyl chains with low-nanomolar inhibitory potency. Their prolonged residence time and minimal catalytic turnover, confirmed by kinetic analysis, support a “slow substrate” inhibition mechanism. Ternary crystal structures of SIRT2−peptide−NAD+ complexes are consistent with a rate-limiting initial nucleophilic attack of the amide oxygen on NAD+. The inhibitors stabilize a catalytically competent yet unproductive enzyme state, distinct from thiocarbonyl inhibitors that form stalled intermediates with NAD+. Comparative structural and biochemical analyses with SIRT1 and SIRT3 reveal isoform-specific acyl chain trajectories underlying selectivity. Extension to potentially naturally occurring or drug-derived Nε-lysine modifications, i.e., phytanoyl- and ibuprofenyl-lysine, demonstrates that diverse branched acyl groups inhibit SIRT2. In cells, optimized inhibitors show low-nanomolar target engagement and induce robust α-tubulin hyperacetylation, establishing slow substrate inhibition as a strategy for selective sirtuin targeting.

item.title: From Ubiquitination to Proteasome-Directed Recruiting: Emerging Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential in Targeted Protein Degradation
item.description:
Abstract
Targeted protein degradation has transformed drug discovery by enabling selective elimination of disease-associated proteins. Beyond classical E3 ligase-recruiting degraders, emerging proteasome-directed strategies seek to recruit targets directly to the proteasome, potentially bypassing E3 ligase dependency and ubiquitination requirements. This approach may expand the degradable proteome, but requires proteasome ligands that engage accessible surfaces, tolerate linker attachment, and preserve basal proteasome function. In this Perspective, we summarize recent advances in direct proteasome-targeting degradation, focusing on ligands of the 19S regulatory particle and 20S core particle. We assess how proteasome subunits and binding pockets have been exploited for degrader design and distinguish ligand-level challenges, such as undefined binding sites, immature SAR, and uncertain linker vectors, from degrader-level issues, including cellular exposure, degradation selectivity, off-target effects, and proteostasis liability. These considerations provide a framework for designing next-generation proteasome-recruiting degraders.

item.title: Reducing off-Target hERG Activity of First-Generation DCN1-UBE2M Interaction Inhibitors: Design, Synthesis, and Structure−Activity Relationships
item.description:
Abstract
We previously reported a potent and orally available inhibitor (2, NAcM-OPT) of the DCN1-UBE2M protein interaction that targets the neddylation pathway to potentially regulate oncogenic transformation for the treatment of cancer. In vivo profiling of compound 2 revealed that, while it was potent, orally bioavailable, and inhibited growth of tumor xenografts in immunodeficient mice, it possessed significant off-target affinity for the human ether-a-go-go-related gene protein (hERG Ki = 750 nM), thereby significantly limiting its potential for development. Herein, we disclose the rational and systematic modification of compound 2 to reduce the affinity for hERG while maintaining its affinity for and activity against DCN1. These studies led to the discovery of compound 110, which exhibited equivalent biochemical and cellular potency to 2, improved physicochemical properties, and increased selectivity relative to hERG.

item.title: Centromere-Targeting Chimeras for Combating Cancer Drug Resistance
item.description:
Abstract
Centromere protein B (CENPB), the only sequence-specific DNA-binding protein at centromeres, maintains chromosomal stability and accurate mitotic segregation. Its overexpression in aggressive cancers is associated with aneuploidy and poor prognosis, yet CENPB remains therapeutically underexplored because direct inhibitors are unavailable. Here, we develop CENPB OligoTAC, a DNA-based PROTAC comprising a CENPB-binding oligodeoxynucleotide linked to an E3 ligase ligand. CENPB OligoTAC induces ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of CENPB, disrupting centromere integrity, causing chromosome mis-segregation, and activating apoptosis. It shows potent activity in preclinical non-small cell lung cancer models resistant to first-, second-, and third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors, while exhibiting minimal cytotoxicity toward normal cells and good serum stability. In vivo, CENPB OligoTAC demonstrates favorable pharmacokinetics, good tolerability, and no significant hematological changes. By exploiting cancer cells’ dependence on centromeric stability, this platform offers a novel strategy for selectively targeting aneuploid malignancies.

item.title: FGFR3 Selectivity in Drug Discovery: Biological Rationale, Design Strategies, and Therapeutic Potential
item.description:
Abstract
Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gain-of-function alterations drive a spectrum of conditions, including cancers and skeletal dysplasias, making FGFR3 an attractive therapeutic target. While second-generation pan-FGFR inhibitors established clinical proof-of-concept, their utility has been constrained by toxicities associated with inhibition of FGFR1, FGFR2, and FGFR4. Despite the high degree of structural homology within the FGFR family, structure-guided medicinal chemistry efforts have recently enabled the development of the first FGFR3-selective inhibitors to enter clinical evaluation. These agents are now being investigated for indications including bladder cancer and achondroplasia. Improved isoform selectivity has the potential to enhance tolerability, enable more durable target inhibition, and expand the therapeutic application of FGFR3-directed therapies. In this Perspective, we discuss the biological rationale for selective FGFR3 inhibition, the structure-based design strategies that have enabled FGFR3 selectivity, and emerging clinical opportunities to address unmet needs in FGFR3-driven disease.

item.title: Discovery of a Pyrazine-2-Carboxamide Derivative as a Potent Plasmodium falciparum Inhibitor with Potential for Single-Dose Cure
item.description:
Abstract
Malaria remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly among young children, in endemic regions such as sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia. Moreover, the emerging resistance of Plasmodium parasites to front-line therapeutics underscores the need for new blood-stage antimalarial drugs. Utilizing a Plasmodium falciparum (Pf) growth inhibition assay, we identified a novel pyrazine-2-carboxamide series. Lead optimization improved anti-plasmodial potency, metabolic stability, and reduced CYP2D6 inhibition risk, leading to the selection of IWY357 (1). A single dose of 100 mg per kg (mpk) is fully curative in a Pf-humanized severe combined immunodeficient mouse model (TADhuMouse®-Pfalc), and IWY357 (1) also exhibits a high barrier to resistance in drug selection studies. Given the significant potential to provide a curative therapy for uncomplicated malaria with short dosing regimens, either alone or in combination, IWY357 (1) was progressed through GLP toxicology studies into phase 1 clinical trials.

item.title: Evaluation of Cytotoxic Potential of Water-Soluble Photosensitive Pincer-Copper Complexes
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, the synthesis and characterization of four new water-soluble pincer-copper complexes of the type (R2NNN)CuCl2 (R = C6H5, p-OMe-C6H4, p-Me-C6H4, and p-F-C6H4) based on bis(imino)pyridine ligands have been reported. The complexes exhibited significant cytotoxicity against a monolayer of MCF-7 breast cancer cells following light irradiation. Notably, the complex (Ph2NNN)CuCl2 demonstrated the highest efficacy among the pincer-Cu complexes, with an IC50 of 11 μM in the presence of light and an IC50 of 25 μM in dark conditions, making it ideal for photodynamic therapy (PDT). The complex (Ph2NNN)CuCl2 demonstrated selectivity for MCF-7 cells, as indicated by its reduced cytotoxicity against HEK cells. The generation of singlet oxygen (1O2) led to photo-oxidation-mediated apoptosis, as evidenced by the Annexin V/PI assay and concomitant G2/M cell cycle arrest. Furthermore, cleaved PARP (cPARP) expression upon photoactivation also confirmed the induction of apoptosis. This work provides an avenue for future applications of strategically engineered water-soluble pincer-metal complexes in cancer phototherapy.

item.title: Ligands Targeting α9-Containing Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptors: Structure−Activity Relationships and Therapeutic Potential in Neuropathic Pain
item.description:
Abstract
Neuropathic pain remains a significant clinical challenge due to the varying efficacies and aversive effects associated with the currently available treatments. Most notably, the addiction potential associated with opioid use for pain presents a critical need for non-opioid-targeting analgesics. In the last two decades, α9-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) have been evaluated preclinically for their potential as a new target for neuropathic pain therapies. In this perspective, we discuss several classes of ligands that modulate these receptors, highlighting hurdles that have arisen during their development and efforts that have been made to improve their therapeutic potential. Additionally, we consider the significant role these ligands have played in current and future drug discovery for this target.

item.title: Cascade Mono- and Di-Functionalization of Anticancer Diastereomeric Benzoxazole-Ansamycins toward the Development of Highly Potent Hsp90 Inhibitors of Decreased Toxicity in Normal Cells
item.description:
Abstract
To reduce toxicity of geldanamycin (GDM), the domino transformation of its benzoquinone core into benzoxazole has been performed. Structural studies of ester-phenol and ester-ether benzoxazole-type ansamycins indicate that the former is present as (Sp)-diastereomer, whereas the latter is present as conformation-“locked” (Rp)-diastereomer, which is more favorable at binding to Hsp90. Several of the obtained benzoxazole ansamycins revealed high anticancer potency in SKBr-3, MCF-7, SKOV-3, and PC-3 lines with improved selectivity and lower affinity to glutathione, compared to GDM. The most potent derivative 6 reveals excellent anticancer activity (IC50 < 0.6 μM) with Hsp90 as the primary target [KD6-Hsp90 = 0.3 μM], limited off-target effects (kinases), and decreased toxicity (selectivity indices = 2.75−3.48) regarding GDM. Ester-ether type derivative 22 reveals good anticancer potency in SKOV-3 (IC50 = 0.62 μM) with reduced toxicity in human dermal fibroblast and human umbilical vein endothelial cells, improved selectivity (SISKOV-3 = 2.75), apoptotic index AISKOV-3 ∼8, and high chemical and in vivo stabilities.

item.title: Discovery of Epoxysuccinates as Potent Covalent Inhibitors of SARS-CoV-2 Papain-like Protease
item.description:
Abstract
The papain-like protease (PLpro) of SARS-CoV-2, essential for viral processing and immune evasion, is a promising therapeutic target for coronavirus infections. Incorporating strategies used to enhance activity of non-covalent inhibitors, notably engagement of the BL2-groove, remote from the active site Cys-111, covalent PLpro inhibitors were designed. Epoxysuccinamide inhibitors demonstrated subnanomolar potency and 107-fold reduction in viral titer in cell cultures. The flexible hydrazide linker required for reaction of Cys-111 with the epoxysuccinamide warhead was susceptible to hepatic carboxylesterase metabolism. Replacement of hydrazide with alternative linkers was unsuccessful. Administered i.v., an epoxysuccinamide was well tolerated in mice. Although metabolically limited for targeting SARS-CoV-2 PLpro, the warhead was validated as a potent tool in the armamentarium of antivirals to confront emerging viruses.

item.title: gem -Dimethylcarbinol: A tert -Butyl Bioisostere with Greatly Reduced Lipophilicity
item.description:
Abstract
The tert-butyl group is a large substituent that could be useful in some contexts for filling protein pockets, but this highly lipophilic group typically worsens the ADMET properties of the parent scaffold. Although many bioisosteres of tert-butyl are similarly lipophilic, gem-dimethylcarbinol could be a bioisostere with greatly reduced lipophilicity, bestowing balanced properties to a lead compound. This could benefit multi-parameter optimization that includes solubility, permeability, and in vitro clearance. Although one downside of installing the gem-dimethylcarbinol group is greater efflux, making it a poor motif for CNS applications, small structural modifications could mitigate this issue. The gem-dimethylcarbinol group is not chemically reactive under physiological conditions, is not a blacklisted toxicophore, and is present in a small but growing number of approved drugs. Furthermore, the simplicity of its installation in organic chemistry makes it an attractive option as a tert-butyl bioisostere with great opportunities in medicinal chemistry.

item.title: De Novo Design of Multi-Mechanistic AIE Photosensitizer for Broad-Spectrum Bacterial Eradication
item.description:
Abstract
Antibiotic resistance poses a serious threat to human health. Inspired by the clinical practice of employing drug combinations to achieve combined effects, we hypothesized that integrating multiple mechanisms into a single molecule could address drug-resistant bacterial infections. Based on a propeller-modification strategy and dual alkyl-chain engineering, we de novo designed and synthesized a C2-symmetric propeller-shaped aggregation-induced emission photosensitizer. After iterative screening, the optimized compound MeOTDP-2 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, enabling efficient eradication of planktonic bacteria, drug-resistant strains, polymicrobial infections, biofilms, and persister cells, with no cellular invasiveness and negligible cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies revealed that MeOTDP-2 achieves chemo-photodynamic combined antibacterial therapy by targeting and disrupting bacterial membranes and DNA, alongside light-mediated intracellular reactive oxygen species accumulation. Furthermore, in mouse models of MRSA-induced skin abscess and full-thickness skin wound infection, MeOTDP-2 demonstrated superior therapeutic efficacy to vancomycin. This strategy, integrating dual targeting with multiple mechanisms, offers new promise for overcoming bacterial resistance.

item.title: Recent Advances in Peptide−Oligonucleotide Conjugates for Enhanced Therapeutic Efficacy
item.description:
Abstract
Oligonucleotide therapeutics have emerged as next-generation therapeutics. However, targeted delivery of oligonucleotides to extrahepatic tissues, such as skeletal and cardiac muscles and the central nervous system, at efficacious yet well-tolerated doses remain a major challenge for their clinical translation. Although antibody−oligonucleotide conjugates are promising for the treatment of genetic disorders, inadequate tissue penetration and immunogenicity have constrained their therapeutic efficacy. By combining the advantages of cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) or cell-targeting peptides (CTPs) with those of oligonucleotides, peptide−oligonucleotide conjugates (POCs) display enhanced cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and extrahepatic delivery. The therapeutic efficacy of POC was increased through conjugation with CPPs, endosomal-escape peptides (EEPs), fusogenic peptides, nuclear localization signal peptides, or CTPs. In this perspective, innovative molecular designs such as multivalent, cyclic, and chimeric peptides, and combinations of CPPs and EEPs, were explored, highlighting key advancements in POC development and providing insights into future directions for the development of novel POCs.

item.title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of Pentacyclic Triterpene Derivatives as Intestinal FXR Antagonists for Type 2 Diabetes
item.description:
Abstract
Intestinal farnesoid X receptor (FXR) antagonism has emerged as a strategy to enhance endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) secretion and improve metabolic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Dihydrooleanolic acid methyl ester (DKS26) served as the scaffold for the synthesis of 64 pentacyclic triterpene derivatives modified at the terminal carboxyl group and C-3/C-12 positions. Esterification of the terminal carboxylate emerged as a determinant of FXR antagonism, identifying 4l bearing a tetrazole-containing side chain and C-12 hydroxyl motif. Compound 4l antagonized FXR in a TR-FRET assay (IC50 = 11.79 μM), a fivefold improvement over DKS26. In NCI-H716 cells, 4l reduced NR0B2 (SHP) mRNA expression and markedly stimulated GLP-1 secretion. In HFD/STZ-induced diabetic mice, oral 4l improved glycemia, increased circulating GLP-1 and insulin, and alleviated dyslipidemia and organ injury markers. These findings establish the pentacyclic triterpene scaffold as a platform for FXR antagonism and identify 4l as a lead for further optimization.

item.title: A Novel Small-Molecule Antagonist of the NOD1 Signaling Pathway as a Therapeutic Strategy for Acute Pancreatitis
item.description:
Abstract
Acute pancreatitis (AP) is a sterile inflammatory disease characterized by aberrant zymogen activation, tissue autodigestion, and cross-amplifying inflammatory cascades that complicate targeted therapies. Our single-cell transcriptomics analysis revealed early NOD1 pathway activation in pancreatic acinar and ductal cells in cerulein-induced AP mice, suggesting potential involvement across these cell types. Here, through a scaffold-hopping strategy, we obtained novel-scaffold NOD1 antagonists. Further optimization yielded 32q and its highly water-soluble disodium salt, 32q-2Na. They exhibited low-nanomolar potency against NOD1 with high selectivity. 32q-2Na pharmacologically inhibited NOD1 signaling, significantly reducing serum levels of amylase (AMY), lipase (LIP), MCP-1, and IL-6, and markedly attenuating pancreatic inflammatory responses in cerulein- and FAEE-induced murine models of AP. In conclusion, these findings establish NOD1 as a highly tractable upstream regulatory node for AP intervention.

item.title: Enhancing the Specificity of the CAIX-Targeted Radionuclide Probe via the Optimization Cyclic Peptide Cyclization Linker
item.description:
Abstract
Carbonic anhydrase IX (CAIX) is a key biomarker for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) PET imaging. The reported probe 68Ga-DPI-4452 strongly targets both hCAIX and hCAII, therefore hindering its clinical applications. This study developed two optimized probes, 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2. They have nanomolar affinity for hCAIX but far weaker binding to hCAII compared with that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. In OS-RC-2 tumor-bearing mice, the tumor uptake of 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 was comparable to that of 68Ga-DPI-4452. However, since 68Ga-WF2 exhibited the lowest affinity for mCAII and mCAIX, its gastrointestinal uptake was the lowest. The autoradiography result revealed that three probes strongly bound human ccRCC tissues, while 68Ga-WF1 and 68Ga-WF2 bound far less to digestive tract tissues. Due to the lowest affinity of 68Ga-WF1 for hCAII, it effectively reduces uptake in the human gastrointestinal tract, holding promise for high tumor contrast and low gastrointestinal tract toxicity for ccRCC PET imaging.

item.title: Exploring the Relationship between Cell Permeability, Intracellular Exposure, and Target Engagement for PROTACs
item.description:
Abstract
Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) occupy beyond-rule-of-5 chemical space, where cellular activity depends on molecular recognition, membrane permeation and unbound exposure at the target site. Here, we examined how these properties shape apparent E3 ligase target engagement for 20 PROTACs spanning different E3 ligase ligands, linkers, and target-binding ligands. Intracellular NanoBRET assays showed a wide range of IC50 values for competition with cereblon or VHL tracer binding when referenced to externally applied concentrations. Passive Caco-2 permeability related only weakly to these values. Recalculating IC50 values using measured intracellular unbound exposure narrowed the spread from approximately 4000-fold to 150-fold, in quantitative agreement with IC50 values measured directly in permeabilized cells. Thus, much of the apparent variation in target engagement reflects differential intracellular exposure rather than intrinsic E3 ligase recognition, and incorporating unbound exposure provides a more mechanistic basis for interpreting cellular target engagement data and distinguishing exposure-driven effects from genuine structure−activity relationships.

item.title: Dual Peptide Modification via Isopeptide Bonding and Lipidation Boosts Antifungal Activity
item.description:
Abstract
The rapid rise in drug-resistant infectious diseases urgently demands new therapeutic strategies, particularly against fungi. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are key effectors of innate immunity in all organisms, killing various microorganisms. Despite their potential, few AMPs effectively target pathogens without harming the host. Here, we incorporated isopeptide bonds and lipophilic acids into AMPs, forming lipo-isopeptides (LIIPs). LIIPs were active against diverse microorganisms, predominantly Candida albicans (C. albicans), and exhibited improved protease resistance. These modifications altered the secondary structure and oligomerization behavior, while enhancing membrane affinity. Consequently, by coating surfaces and cells, the non-toxic C8-Amp1EP reduces fungal adhesion and biofilm formation, and acts by disrupting and depolarizing the C. albicans membrane at both planktonic and biofilm stages. Importantly, under serial-passage conditions, C8-Amp1EP showed a lower propensity to induce resistance than conventional antifungal treatments. These findings identify LIIPs as promising, selective agents for combating infections, paving the way for future therapeutic development.

item.title: Discovery of Potent, Orally Bioavailable, and CNS-Penetrant 1,2,3-Triazolopyridinyl Piperazine-Based PARP1-Selective Inhibitors
item.description:
Abstract
Hematological toxicities have resulted in limiting the dose of first-generation PARP inhibitors, which have activity at both PARP1 and PARP2. With the advancement of selective PARP1 inhibitors to the clinic, we embarked on a program to identify novel PARP1 inhibitors that are suitable for the treatment of CNS malignancies. Central to our design was the replacement of the carboxamide in saruparib with a series of heterocycles. Our progression criteria included using Caco-2 efflux instead of the more commonly used MDR1-MDCK efflux to enable identifying compounds with Kpu,u >0.3. This work culminated in the discovery of the potent, selective, orally bioavailable, and CNS-penetrant PARP1 inhibitor 33, which demonstrated tumor growth inhibition and regression in xenograft models at 0.2 mg/kg QD. Predicted human PK parameters coupled with a tumor growth PKPD model for 33 estimated an efficacious clinical dose of <150 mg once daily.

item.title: Design, Synthesis and Dual-Stage Antimalarial Evaluation of β-Carboline−Metronidazole Hybrids: Structure−Activity Relationship and Molecular Docking Correlations
item.description:
Abstract
Malaria remains a major global health challenge, exacerbated by emerging drug-resistant Plasmodium strains. Herein, we report the design, synthesis, and dual-stage antimalarial evaluation of β-carboline−metronidazole hybrids. The synthesized hybrids, linked through ester and amide bonds, were evaluated in vitro against chloroquine-sensitive (Pf3D7) and resistant (PfK1) Plasmodium falciparum strains, as well as liver-stage Plasmodium berghei. Several compounds exhibited potent blood-stage inhibition (IC50 as low as 0.05 ± 0.02 μM), remarkable liver-stage activity surpassing primaquine, and favourable selectivity indices (>100). Notably, compound 8kkk achieved up to 95% suppression of parasitemia in P. berghei ANKA-infected Swiss mice at 50 mg/kg for four days. Pharmacokinetic studies revealed a distinct absorption and disposition profile. SAR analysis highlighted the importance of electronic nature and substitution pattern of the β-carboline scaffold, while molecular docking and fluorimetry analysis indicated strong binding to PfLDH. These findings suggest β-carboline−metronidazole hybrids as promising candidates for further development as dual-stage antimalarial agents.

item.title: Next-Generation Neutral Sphingomyelinase-2 Inhibitors with Improved Solubility, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy in a Tau Propagation Model
item.description:
Abstract
Neutral sphingomyelinase 2 (nSMase2) is a promising therapeutic target implicated in disease progression. We previously identified PDDC [phenyl (R)-(1-(3-(3,4-dimethoxyphenyl)-2,6-dimethylimidazo[1,2-b]pyridazin-8-yl)-pyrrolidin-3-yl) carbamate], a sub-micromolar nSMase2 inhibitor with favorable efficacy and pharmacokinetics in mice. However, poor aqueous solubility and suboptimal pharmacokinetics in higher species limited its translational potential. To overcome these limitations, we introduced hydroxy groups on the southern phenyl ring and simultaneously optimized the northern phenyl-carbamate moiety. Compound 8a [(phenyl (R)-(1-(3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2,6-dimethylimidazo[1,2-b]pyridazin-8-yl)pyrrolidin-3-yl) carbamate] exhibited comparable potency and pharmacokinetics to PDDC but remained poorly soluble. To address this, we derivatized the hydroxy group with hydrophilic phosphate promoeities, generating soluble analogues of 8a. Of these, 12a demonstrated excellent aqueous solubility and efficiently released 8a, resulting in improved pharmacokinetics, target engagement, and efficacy in mice. In dogs, oral dosing of 12a resulted in the release of 8a, with the released 8a exhibiting 47% absolute oral bioavailability, supporting its translational potential.

item.title: Site-Specific Bioconjugation in Antibody−Drug Conjugates: From Conjugation Chemistry to Precision Molecular Design
Discovery of C5-Substituted 2′-Fluorinated Pyrimidine Nucleosides as Potent and Orally Efficacious Anti-HSV Agents
item.description:
Abstract
Herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections remain a significant global health concern. Through phenotypic screening of a nucleoside-focused library followed by systematic structure−activity relationship (SAR) explorations, we identified C5-substituted 2′-fluorinated pyrimidine nucleosides as promising anti-HSV scaffolds. We found that introducing five-membered heteroaryls at the uracil C5 position significantly enhanced antiviral potency, whereas cytosine and alkynyl derivatives showed limited efficacy. The optimized lead, B10, exhibited potent in vitro inhibition against HSV-1 (EC50 = 0.60 μM) and HSV-2 (EC50 = 7.32 μM) with minimal cytotoxicity. Importantly, B10 demonstrated a highly favorable oral bioavailability of 48.0% in rats. In a murine intranasal HSV-1 infection model, oral administration of B10 significantly improved survival rates, alleviated weight loss, suppressed acute viral replication in the central nervous system, and reduced pulmonary viral titers. These findings highlight the 2′-fluoro-C5-heteroaryl uracil framework as a robust chemotype and establish B10 as an orally efficacious candidate for HSV therapy.

item.title: Development of Long-Acting Teriparatide Analogues through Iterative Peptide Scanning and Site-Specific Modification by Serine/Threonine Ligation
item.description:
Abstract
Teriparatide, the only FDA-approved osteoanabolic drug for osteoporosis, suffers from poor metabolic stability and requires frequent subcutaneous injections, leading to suboptimal patient compliance. To find optimized teriparatide derivatives, we herein report an iterative peptide scanning strategy followed by a serine/threonine ligation (STL) chemistry for site-specific modifications. Using our 2-hydroxyphenol-pseudoproline (ψ2-hydroxyphenolpro) modification (HPM) method, two series of teriparatide analogues with different types of substituents were successfully prepared for scanning the modifiable sites and their expansibility. Through chemoselective acylation of embedded serine/threonine residues, several fatty acids of unequal lengths were introduced to further improve the pharmacokinetic properties of scanning derivatives. Among the 12 lipidated analogues, 54, 55, 62, and 63 exhibited potent antiosteoporotic activities in vitro and in vivo close to those of native teriparatide. The most effective compound, 62, also demonstrated significantly enhanced serum stability and may serve as a promising candidate for further development of long-acting antiosteoporotic pharmaceuticals.

item.title: A Novel Chemotype of Orally Active SARS-CoV-2 NSP14 Methyltransferase Inhibitors
item.description:
Abstract
The periodic emergence of human coronaviruses (hCoVs) necessitates direct-acting antivirals targeting underexploited viral proteins with broad-spectrum potential. Building on our discovery of TDI-015051, a first-in-class SARS-CoV-2 mRNA cap guanine-N7 methyltransferase (MTase) NSP14 inhibitor whose translational development was limited by metabolic liabilities, we conducted medicinal chemistry optimization of a structurally distinct high-throughput screening hit. We arrived at MAVDA-K-256, a small-molecule inhibitor with improved pharmacological properties compared to TDI-015051. MAVDA-K-256 engaged NSP14 through the formation of a ternary complex with S-adenosyl-l-homocysteine, potently inhibiting its MTase activity and SARS-CoV-2 replication (EC50 = 24.6 nM). MAVDA-K-256 demonstrated broad-spectrum antiviral activity against diverse hCoVs without targeting the host mRNA cap MTase. Its favorable metabolic stability and pharmacokinetic properties enabled twice-daily oral dosing in a murine SARS-CoV-2 infection model, resulting in a five-log reduction in viral lung burden. These findings validate NSP14 inhibition as a promising antiviral strategy and support further preclinical development of MAVDA-K-256.

item.title: A Modular Peptide Strategy for Targeted Lysosomal Degradation of TGF-βR1
item.description:
Abstract
Direct depletion of TGF-βR1 may provide more durable suppression of profibrotic signaling than occupancy-driven inhibition, but compact lysosome-directed degraders remain underdeveloped. Here, we report a peptide-based strategy for lysosomal degradation of TGF-βR1 by re-engineering a caveolin-derived antifibrotic scaffold. Structure-guided optimization identified T19 as an improved TGF-βR1-directed sequence, and incorporation of an intrinsic lysosome-targeting module generated P2, which induced time and dose-dependent, lysosome-dependent TGF-βR1 downregulation. Fatty-acid conjugation afforded P2-FA with improved stability and pharmacokinetic properties. P2-FA suppressed profibrotic signaling, reduced α-SMA and COL1A1 expression, and inhibited proliferation and migration of activated LX-2 cells. In a CCl4-induced mouse model, P2-FA attenuated collagen deposition, decreased fibrotic marker expression, and alleviated liver injury. These results identify P2-FA as a pharmacologically improved peptide-based TGF-βR1 degrader and antifibrotic lead.

item.title: Development of a Potent and Isoform-Selective HDAC11 Inhibitor with Anti-Tumor Efficacy against Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
Targeting histone deacetylase 11 (HDAC11) represents a promising therapeutic strategy, yet developing selective inhibitors for solid tumors remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we describe the rational lead optimization of a novel series of indole-based hydroxamic acids. Guided by our previous lead PB94, a systematic, multiparameter optimization of the core, linker, and cap regions was conducted to specifically target HDAC11. This campaign yielded compound YP200, which incorporates a precisely positioned secondary amine linker and an adamantane surface-recognition cap. YP200 exhibited exceptional HDAC11 inhibitory potency (IC50 = 0.058 ± 0.01 μM) and good selectivity (>103-fold) over other HDACs. Furthermore, YP200 demonstrated good in vivo anti-tumor efficacy in a non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patient-derived xenograft model. These findings validate YP200 as a promising HDAC11-targeted therapeutic candidate, significantly expanding the therapeutic arsenal for solid tumors.

item.title: Alpha-Lipoic Acid Derivatives: A Multifunctional Neuroprotective Agent with Potential for Treating Ischemic Stroke
item.description:
Abstract
Ischemic stroke (IS) is a major public health burden due to its high mortality and disability rates. Neuroinflammation and ferroptosis are two key drivers of IS progression. α-Lipoic acid (ALA) exhibits both anti-ferroptosis and anti-inflammatory activities; however, its anti-ferroptosis efficacy is suboptimal. In this study, we designed and synthesized 23 ALA derivatives. Among them, D14 exhibited the most potent anti-ferroptosis activity, with an EC50 value of 0.00247 μM, an approximately 16,000-fold improvement over ALA, while retaining comparable anti-inflammatory activity (IC50 = 13.6 μM). Mechanistically, D14 scavenged free radicals and activated the Nrf2/GPX4 pathway to restore GSH levels and reduce MDA, Fe2+, and ROS accumulation, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis. D14 also suppressed NF-κB activation by preventing IκBα degradation and p65 phosphorylation, and it reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α secretion. In a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model, D14 reduced cerebral infarct volume and ameliorated neurological deficits, surpassing ALA and the clinically used drug edaravone. Preliminary toxicity evaluation of D14 indicated a favorable safety profile. Overall, D14 is a promising multi-target lead compound for the treatment of IS.

item.title: Potent and Cell Active 5-Azaindole-based Tau Tubulin Kinase Inhibitors Disrupt Ciliogenesis
item.description:
Abstract
We have characterized a potent and cell active tau tubulin kinase 1 and 2 (TTBK1 and TTBK2) inhibitor, 13. Analysis of the in-cell, kinome-wide selectivity of compound 13 revealed it to only bind five of 300 kinases with >50% occupancy at 1 μM: CDK11B, CDK11A, CK1δ, CK1ε, and EPHA2. Extensive dose−response follow-up studies in cells refined the off-target kinases of compound 13 to include CDK11B, CDK11A, CK1δ, and PIKfyve based on their NanoBRET IC50 values being <1 μM. As part of our medicinal chemistry campaign, we also identified a structurally similar negative control, compound 5, which lacks in-cell affinity for TTBK1 and TTBK2. TTBK2 is an effector of ciliogenesis, acting in concert with CEP164, CP110, and CEP83 to initiate the biogenesis of primary cilia. We demonstrate that compound 13 ablates TTBK2 autophosphorylation and significantly disrupts ciliogenesis in hTERT-RPE-1 cells, making it a powerful tool compound for ciliary studies.

item.title: Rethinking log P : Lipophilicity =̷ Hydrophobicity
item.description:
Abstract
LogP values have served as cutoffs for hit-, lead-, and drug-likeness as well as thresholds for toxicity and ADME decision-making and are often characterized as lipophilicity. When the properties of octanol and the experimental limitations of logP measurements are considered, it becomes clear that logP > 3 must be due to increased hydrophobicity and not lipophilicity. We propose that the partition coefficient between either octanol or water and “the thermodynamic ideal solution” is a useful reference to separately determine octanol solvation (lipophilicity) and aqueous solvation (hydrophilicity). We further propose that the ideal solubility of solids measures “autophilicity”. Aqueous solvation spans many orders of magnitude, yet octanol solvation is much narrower, and thus lipophilicity is nearly constant. Understanding which molecules are hydrophobic, rather than lipophilic, can be critical in interpreting affinity, PK, ADME, safety, and other behaviors of molecules necessitating these more nuanced definitions.

item.title: Ligand-Dependent Affinity but State-Dominated Efficacy in Structure-Based GPCR Pharmacology Prediction
item.description:
Abstract
High accuracy in structure-based prediction of G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) efficacy may reflect the receptor state rather than ligand-specific information. We addressed these information sources using state rules, ligand-blind baselines, matched receptor-state contrasts, ligand permutation, and out-of-distribution (OOD) evaluation, with affinity prediction as a positive control. State rules and ligand-blind geometry achieved binary-efficacy-balanced accuracies of 0.844−0.910 and 0.777−0.870, respectively. Of 75 ligand-aware evaluations, 72 failed at least one prespecified ligand-sensitivity condition, and three lacked required evidence; none met all required criteria. Affinity pretraining gave no detectable efficacy benefit over matched random initialization. In contrast, ligand chemistry supported affinity prediction across 14,740 measured pairs, and all 12 primary affinity permutation comparisons deteriorated, although this advantage did not persist under scaffold, family, or combined OOD splits. Accuracy on endpoint structures therefore cannot alone establish ligand-specific efficacy learning; the findings do not set a general limit on such learning.

item.title: The Phenotypic Hit-to-Probe Challenge
item.description:
Abstract
Phenotypic drug discovery (PDD) fuels the clinical pipelines with first-in-class therapeutic modalities. Success rates depend on the quality of the assay models and can be hampered by resource-intensive processes of target and mode-of-action deconvolution. A critical part of this practice is generating focused sets of phenotypic probes to accelerate in vivo validation and to support target/concept tractability and translatability, raising the question of which phenotypic hit analogues to synthesize as high-quality chemical probes for a given campaign. Here, we outline recommendations and discuss criteria tailored to the specific demands of phenotypic probes. With examples of successful PDD programs, some of which have yielded approved first-in-class drugs, we illustrate common design principles. These underscore that phenotypic probes benefit from (a) availability of matched pairs of active/inactive stereoisomers, (b) ligand topology-guided optimization, and (c) exit vectors for ADME- and target deconvolution-driven acceleration of early in vivo proof-of-concept and advancement towards clinical candidates.

item.title: Discovery of Anti-apoptotic BAX Inhibitors
item.description:
Abstract
BAX is a critical regulator of the apoptosis cascade and its abnormal activation contributes to the development of disease including cardiovascular and neurodegenerative disorders. Therefore, BAX represents an attractive target for the pharmacological inhibition of pathological cell death. Based on a virtual screen, we identified and modified several EGFR kinase inhibitors with potential activity against BAX. Systematic modifications of the dacomitinib and gefitinib core structure were performed, allowing us to elucidate how structural modifications influence biological activity and leading to a comprehensive structure-activity relationship (SAR) on BAX inhibition. The developed series has favorable drug-like properties and improved BAX inhibitory activity in vitro, in cells, and in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived brain organoids, with significantly reduced EGFR kinase activity. This series therefore represents a promising starting point for the development of improved and potentially therapeutic BAX inhibitors.

item.title: FDA Approval of Ensitrelvir: an Oral, Nonpeptidic, Noncovalent SARS-CoV-2 Main Protease Inhibitor for Household Postexposure Prophylaxis
item.description: John D. Stobo, M.D. Distinguished Chair EndowmentN/ANational Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of HealthT32 AI15538505

item.title: FAP-Triggered In Situ Self-Assembly of HPQ in Tumors Empowers 131 I Internal Radiotherapy
item.description:
Abstract
Fibroblast activating protein (FAP) is specifically overexpressed in malignant tumors. The 2-(2′-hydroxyphenyl)-4(3H)-quinazolinone (HPQ) scaffold exhibits hydrophobicity, aggregation-induced emission (AIE). The responsive probes built on HPQ can undergo in situ activation and self-assembling precipitation, enabling prolonged retention in lesion sites. Herein, a FAP-cleavable Cbz-Gly-Pro-sequence was conjugated to the phenolic hydroxyl of HPQ via a self-immolative linker, with phenol/tyrosine moieties for 131I labeling through aliphatic linkers, affording LWH-1 and LWH-2. LWH-3 further incorporated a tetraphenylethylene moiety, a PEG6-triazole-PEG6 linker, and (D-Tyr)5-NH2. All precursors for radioiodination responded efficiently to FAP, releasing HPQ-OH to generate AIE and illuminating tumors for over 48 h. [131I]LWH-3 showed a 2.76-fold higher molar activity than [131I]LWH-2 and an in vivo half-life of 43.66 min. In PC12-FAP xenografts, [131I]LWH-3 achieved outstanding antitumor efficacy with favorable biosafety. Transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses revealed that internal radiotherapy attenuated tumor metabolic adaptability by modulating fatty acid metabolism-associated networks to impair proliferation.

item.title: HER2-Targeting Affibody Equipped with Albumin-Binding Small Molecules for Radiotheranostics
item.description:
Abstract
HER2-targeting affibody radioprobes are often limited by rapid systemic clearance and excessive renal accumulation. Herein, we develop a modular chemical strategy to optimize the pharmacokinetic properties of affibodies through conjugation of small-molecule albumin-binding motifs (ABMs). Enabled by our selective S-glycosylation approach, ABMs were introduced via a sugar-based linker, allowing systematic modulation of probe behavior. Evaluation of sugar-modified variants revealed that sugar structure plays a critical role in regulating in vivo distribution, with the GalNAc-modified probe [68Ga]Ga-5c exhibiting favorable tumor-to-background contrast in PET/CT imaging. Further incorporation of ABMs afforded GalNAc-IPBA-functionalized affibody [177Lu]Lu-10a, which achieved an 17-fold extension of circulation half-life, reduced renal accumulation, and maintained efficient tumor targeting. Therapeutically, [177Lu]Lu-10a induced 86.25% tumor growth inhibition with minimal systemic toxicity. This study provides a modular strategy for overcoming pharmacokinetic limitations of affibody-based radiotheranostics.

item.title: Medicinal Chemistry Strategies for Targeting RNA-Binding Proteins: Design, Optimization, and Therapeutic Potential
item.description:
Abstract
RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) are essential regulators of post-transcriptional gene expression whose disruption contributes broadly to tumor initiation, progression, and therapeutic resistance. Through their control of RNA splicing, stability, translation, and epitranscriptomic modification, these proteins orchestrate oncogenic networks that sustain hallmark cancer phenotypes. This central role has stimulated intensive efforts to develop small-molecule RBP inhibitors, yielding mechanistically diverse compounds against m6A pathway components and classical oncogenic RBPs with demonstrated efficacy in preclinical models. However, substantial challenges remain, including achieving high target selectivity, optimizing drug-like properties, and addressing adaptive resistance mechanisms. This article examines recent advances in RBP-targeted therapeutics, highlighting design strategies, structural mechanisms, and key obstacles on the path toward clinical application.

item.title: Discovery and Optimization of Anticancer Dibenzothiazepinones That Target the Ribosome Biogenesis Factor NVL
item.description:
Abstract
Using inducible forward genetics, we recently discovered a dibenzothiazepinone (1) with activity against cancer cells via inhibition of the ribosome biogenesis factor NVL (nuclear valosin-containing protein-like). Herein, we delineate a comprehensive structure−activity relationship (SAR) study that explores the structural space surrounding the dibenzothiazepinone scaffold. A series of 115 analogs were synthesized and evaluated for activity against the colorectal cancer cell line HCT116 and counter-screened against cells CRISPR engineered to express a compound-resistant mutation in NVL. Our initial medicinal chemistry-driven campaign focused on improving potency, metabolic stability, and in vivo exposure and clearance. A fluorescence polarization assay with recombinant human NVL established a correlation between NVL-binding and antiproliferative activity. Cryo-EM structures of human NVL with select inhibitors revealed a binding mode that is consistent with the SAR data. This study led to the in vivo analog 100 (MM927), which we reported to suppress tumor growth in vivo without detectable toxicity via targeting the NVL.

item.title: Structure-Guided Discovery of Orally Bioavailable Allosteric SLC6A19 Inhibitors that Promote Urinary Amino Acid Excretion In Vivo
item.description:
Abstract
SLC6A19 is a sodium-dependent transporter that mediates the absorption of neutral amino acids in the intestine and reabsorption of these amino acids in the kidney. Pharmacological inhibition of SLC6A19 may provide therapeutic benefit by normalizing plasma amino acid levels and potentially reducing renal tubular transport burden. Virtual screening against an allosteric binding pocket observed in the cryo-EM structure of SLC6A19/cinromide (1) identified compound 6 as a promising hit. The cryo-EM structure of SLC6A19/CB3 (2) revealed a second, partially overlapping pocket adjacent to the compound 6 binding site. Analogue design merging these two binding pockets followed by optimization led to compound 20, a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable allosteric SLC6A19 inhibitor. While compound 20 demonstrates an approximately 10-fold rightward potency shift against mouse SLC6A19, it retains good potency against non-human primate SLC6A19. Consistent with the SLC6A19 inhibition mechanism, oral dosing of 20 led to increased urinary amino acid excretion in a dose-dependent manner in human SLC6A19 knock-in mice and wild-type non-human primates.

item.title: Discovery of GTA182, a Novel CNS-Active Tricyclic Amide MTA-Cooperative PRMT5 Inhibitor for MTAP -Deleted Cancers
item.description:
Abstract
Developing central nervous system (CNS) active, MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors for MTAP-deleted malignancies represents a formidable challenge. Here, we report the discovery of GTA182 via structure-based drug design. Multi-parameter optimization balanced single-digit nanomolar potency and >100-fold MTAP-deletion selectivity with dose-proportional pharmacokinetics. Optimized physicochemical properties, and minimal efflux delivered unbound brain concentrations within the efficacious range. Oral GTA182 demonstrated robust MTAP deletion-dependent efficacy, achieving net regression at 30 mg/kg (102% TGI) in MTAP-deleted HCT116 xenografts (versus 41% TGI in WT) alongside 59% regression and extended median survival (>91 days) in the orthotopic U87MG-luc glioblastoma model. In a Phase I trial (CTR20243795), GTA182 was well tolerated, shrank intracranial tumors, and achieved an overall objective response rate (ORR) approaching 30%. These properties establish GTA182 as a promising therapeutic candidate for MTAP-deleted systemic and CNS malignancies.

item.title: Discovery of Tricyclic Oxazinoquinolinone-Based BCL6 PROTAC Degraders with Potent Activity Against Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma
item.description:
Abstract
B-cell lymphoma 6 (BCL6) is a key transcriptional repressor involved in the pathogenesis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). In this study, scaffold hopping of BI-3802 led to compound 1, a new tricyclic BCL6-targeting ligand. Further optimization of linker architecture and CRBN-recruiting motifs led to compound 15, a potent BCL6 PROTAC degrader, which induced rapid and efficient BCL6 degradation in OCI-LY1 cells (DC50 = 5.32 nM) and displayed potent antiproliferative activity in BCL6-dependent DLBCL cells (IC50 = 3.2 nM). BCL6 degradation was CRBN- and proteasome-dependent and was accompanied by G1-phase arrest and increased p21 and p27 expression. Oral administration of 15 inhibited tumor growth in an OCI-LY1 xenograft model (TGI = 84% at 20 mg/kg) and reduced tumor BCL6 and Ki67 levels without appreciable body-weight loss or overt major-organ histopathology. Overall, compound 15 represents a promising BCL6 PROTAC degrader for DLBCL.

item.title: Discovery of Indazole-Based Dual-Pharmacophore Inhibitors of Dengue and Zika Proteases as Promising Antivirals
item.description:
Abstract
Flavivirus outbreaks caused by dengue virus (DENV) and Zika virus (ZIKV) remain a major global health challenge, with no FDA-approved antivirals available. Herein, we designed, synthesized, and evaluated indazole-based dual pharmacophore motifs targeting NS2B-NS3 serine proteases, essential for viral replication. Enzymatic assays revealed nanomolar to sub-micromolar potency, with strong selectivity over host serine proteases, minimizing off-target risks. Biophysical studies showed ligand-induced thermal stabilization, while kinetic and dialysis analyses confirmed a reversible, competitive, non-covalent inhibition mechanism. In DENV-infected Vero CCL-81 cells, several leads exhibited potent antiviral activity with low cytotoxicity. Notably, compound C8 demonstrated low-nanomolar enzyme inhibition against both viruses, translating to complete viral suppression in cells (EC50 = 0.5 μM) with a good selectivity index, underscoring its therapeutic potential. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations supported these findings, revealing key active-site interactions consistent with potency and specificity. Collectively, these results highlight indazole-based dual-pharmacophore inhibitors as promising anti-flaviviral leads.

item.title: Lipid Droplet-Targeted Near-Infrared II Type I AIE Photosensitizer Promotes Ferroptosis by Activating Lipophagy
item.description:
Abstract
Lipophagy, a selective autophagic pathway, maintains lipid homeostasis and contributes to ferroptosis by supplying lipid peroxidation substrates. However, organic photosensitizers that activate lipophagy to promote ferroptosis remain scarce. Herein, we developed a NIR-II emissive photosensitizer (MBTTD) targeting lipid droplets (LDs). Compared with its analogue MBTTA, stronger electron-withdrawing groups bathochromically shifted absorption/emission and tuned excited-state decay, enabling efficient type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and high photothermal conversion efficiency. MBTTD nanoparticles (NPs) localized to LDs upon cellular uptake. Upon 808 nm laser irradiation, MBTTD NP-mediated phototherapy disrupted LDs and induced Rab7-regulated lipophagy, releasing polyunsaturated fatty acids that underwent ROS-driven peroxidation, triggering extensive lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. Concurrently, MBTTD-NP-mediated phototherapy triggered endoplasmic reticulum stress and apoptosis. MBTTD NPs showed favorable biocompatibility and potent therapeutic efficacy in multicellular tumor spheroids. In vivo studies revealed that MBTTD NPs enabled NIR-II imaging-guided phototherapy, suppressing 4T1 tumor growth without significant systemic toxicity.

item.title: Structure-Based Design of HDAC6 Inhibitors Targeting the L2 Pocket: Modulating Autophagy and Liquid−Liquid Phase Separation in Lung Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
We herein describe the structure-based design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a new class of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) inhibitors guided by X-ray crystal structures of our previously identified compounds 13-15. X-ray co-crystal structures of second-generation inhibitors 19b (Subseries I) and 20b (Subseries II) within zHDAC6 CD2 confirmed that these compounds behave as highly potent HDAC6 inhibitors with the ability to engage the S531 residue in the L2 loop HDAC6 catalytic domain. Western-blot analysis confirmed the target engagement in cell-based settings, through the increase of acetylated tubulin levels, without significant variation in the histone acetylation status. Compound 20b extensively reduced the viability of A549 cells in both 2- and 3-dimensional cell cultures, through the activation of pro-autophagic pathways. In addition, HDAC6 inhibition impaired the nucleation of stress-granules, confirming the ability of these compounds to modulate liquid−liquid phase separation, an emerging HDAC6-driven hallmark in cancer.

item.title: Development of N -Hydroxyindole-2-Carboxamides as New Host-Targeted Broad-Spectrum Antiviral Agents Against Human Respiratory Viruses
item.description:
Abstract
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) oxidoreductases are promising targets for host-targeted antiviral agents (HTAs) because of their essential role in protein folding, including the maturation of viral proteins. Human protein disulfide isomerase family member A3 (PDIA3) is involved in the folding of N-glycosylated client proteins, including viral envelope proteins, making it an attractive but underexplored antiviral target. Here, we describe the discovery of a novel N-hydroxyindole-2-carboxamide class of PDIA3 inhibitors, exemplified by compound AV22 (1o), which effectively inhibits PDIA3 activity and exerts broad-spectrum antiviral activity against major human respiratory viruses. Mechanistic studies indicated that AV22 (1o) increased the release of non-infectious coronavirus particles and reduced disulfide bond formation in the coronavirus spike protein, indicating that its antiviral effect stems from interference with PDIA3 activity. This new class of HTAs provides promising leads for drug discovery targeting viral envelope protein maturation vulnerabilities and is suitable for developing new BSAs.

item.title: Discovery of Novel STING Inhibitors for the Treatment of Severe Acute Pancreatitis
item.description:
Abstract
Stimulator of interferon genes (STING) is a promising therapeutic target for severe acute pancreatitis (SAP), but effective small-molecule inhibitors remain limited. Here, structure−activity relationship studies identified compound D4 as a potent STING inhibitor with favorable cellular activity and safety. D4 directly engaged STING, inhibited its oligomerization and downstream TBK1/IRF3 signaling, and restored macrophage phagocytosis, autophagic flux, and mitochondrial function while suppressing NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3(NLRP3)-associated pyroptosis. D4 showed oral exposure with 24.70% bioavailability and no overt toxicity at 1000 mg/kg. In a caerulein/LPS-induced SAP model, D4 markedly reduced pancreatic injury, acinar cell necrosis, inflammatory infiltration, and serum amylase and lipase levels. STING knockdown produced similar protective effects. These findings identify D4 as a promising STING-targeting lead compound for SAP treatment.

item.title: Cinchona Alkaloids-Derived Ammonium Salts for Long-Acting and Sensory-Selective Nerve Blockades
item.description:
Abstract
Local anesthetics (LAs), a type of substance with the ability of blocking nerve fiber conduction, are indispensable in clinical practice for pain relief. However, the duration of action and sensory-motor nerve selectivity of conventional LAs require further optimization. Herein, we wish to report the discovery of novel ammonium salts derived from natural cinchona alkaloids for long-acting and sensory-selective nerve blockades. The bicyclic quincoridine skeleton exhibited superior nerve blockade efficacy compared to acyclic and monocyclic analogs. Compound CLA-1-3 produced prolonged nerve blockade (over 50 h) in the rat sciatic nerve block model, possessing an IC50 value of approximately 0.39 μmol/L for voltage-gated sodium channel inhibition. On the other hand, at a concentration range of 0.30% to 0.60%, compound CLA-3-5 achieved sensory-selective nerve blockade lasting up to 3 h. The candidate molecules and underlying mechanistic insights will be valuable assets for drug development and therapeutic innovation.

item.title: Repurposing Approved Chemotherapeutics as Intrinsic Photosensitizers for Single-Molecule Chemophototherapy
item.description:
Abstract
Chemophototherapy (CPT), combining chemotherapy and photodynamic therapy (PDT), is a promising strategy to enhance anticancer efficacy while reducing systemic toxicity. Many approved drugs contain chromophoric moieties that absorb visible light, suggesting their potential as intrinsic photosensitizers. Herein, we introduce a single-molecule chemophototherapy (SM-CPT) approach based on computational screening of approved anticancer drugs for repurposing as photosensitizers. A curated library of 238 small-molecule drugs was screened using time-dependent density functional theory to identify compounds with favourable photophysical properties. Fifteen candidates were identified, and mitoxantrone, pixantrone, daunorubicin, and epirubicin were selected for experimental validation. All compounds generated reactive oxygen species upon irradiation and showed enhanced cytotoxicity in breast cancer cell models, with up to an order-of-magnitude reduction in half-maximal inhibitory concentration values. The approach was further validated in ovarian cancer models, including platinum-resistant cells and patient-derived ascites, highlighting SM-CPT as a translationally attractive light-activated cancer therapy.

item.title: Rational Design of Near-Infrared Difluoroboron Cyanine Photosensitizers for Lipid Droplet-Targeting Imaging and Tumor Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Specifically disrupting lipid droplets (LDs) is an effective strategy for ablating tumor cells through photodynamic therapy (PDT). However, most reported LD probes possess short excitation/emission wavelengths, limiting tissue penetration, and LD-targeted theranostic probes remain underdeveloped. In this work, we first developed a family of near-infrared (NIR) charge-neutral and lipid droplet-targeting cyanine photosensitizers by systematically introducing heavy atoms (Br/I) at different sites of electrically neutral BF2-bridged cyanine (BCy5). These BCy photosensitizers retain the characteristic near-infrared absorption (>650 nm) and high molar extinction coefficients of classical cyanine dyes while exhibiting good singlet oxygen quantum yields. Notably, BCy5-Br1−BCy5-Br3 nanoparticles with high LD specificity exhibit significant PDT efficacy at submicromolar concentrations and, by inducing oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation (LPO) accumulation, concurrently trigger apoptosis and ferroptosis, effectively suppressing melanoma growth in vivo. This work provides vital insights into design principles and transformation of LD-targeting NIR cyanine photosensitizers for cancer PDT.

item.title: Development of DCL1191 as a Potent, Selective and Orally Bioavailable Inhibitor for Autophagy-Associated Transcription Factor EB (TFEB)
item.description:
Abstract
Transcription factor EB (TFEB) is a promising target for autophagy regulation and cancer therapy, yet it has long been regarded as an undruggable protein. Starting from eltrombopag, an FDA-approved agent that exhibits both thrombopoietin receptor (Tpo-R) agonistic activity and TFEB inhibitory potency, we performed systematic structure−activity relationship optimization and identified DCL1191 as a potent, selective, and orally bioavailable TFEB inhibitor. DCL1191 binds TFEB with a Kd of 80.5 nM and disrupts the TFEB-DNA interaction with an IC50 of 60.5 nM. Computational modeling combined with site-directed mutagenesis elucidated its precise binding mode. DCL1191 exhibits diminished activity toward Tpo-R and MITF. Mechanistically, DCL1191 effectively represses the transcription of TFEB target genes and blocks intracellular autophagic flux. In autophagy-hyperactivated U87 glioblastoma cells, DCL1191 substantially sensitizes tumor cells to temozolomide chemotherapy. Pharmacokinetic evaluation in rats further demonstrated that DCL1191 possesses an i.v. half-life of 16.33 h and satisfactory oral bioavailability of 18.77%.

item.title: Antivirulence Benzothiophenes Inhibit Intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis by Targeting the Sensor Histidine Kinase MprB
item.description:
Abstract
Pulmonary tuberculosis remains one of the most prevalent and threatening infectious diseases. Classical anti-tubercular therapy targets essential enzymes of the pathogen Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), thereby suppressing bacterial growth. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains necessitates alternative therapeutic approaches. Virulence inhibition is a promising strategy that blocks Mtb virulence factors required for survival within host cells. We previously identified a hit compound, BTP15, which protected fibroblasts and THP-1 macrophages from Mtb-induced cell death ex vivo by blocking phagosomal escape through inhibition of the mycobacterial histidine kinase MprB. Due to poor pharmacokinetics, the structure of BTP15 was optimized. New benzothiophene derivatives were screened for MprB inhibition, microsomal stability, toxicity, and ex vivo efficacy in THP-1 and MRC-5 cells. The lead compound, 7a, exhibited favorable pharmacokinetic parameters, showed no toxicity in mice at 250 mg/kg, and prevented Mtb dissemination in an acute mouse model of tuberculosis.

item.title: Developing a Ferric(III) Agent for Targeted Inhibition of Growth and Metastasis of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Based on Human Serum Albumin by Chemodynamic Therapy-Driven Synergistic Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) remains challenging due to its aggressiveness and the lack of targeted therapies. In this study, we proposed designing a ferric (Fe) agent based on human serum albumin (HSA) for chemodynamic therapy-driven synergistic therapy. To this end, we not only optimized a series of Fe(III) compounds to obtain Fe4, which has remarkable toxicity against TNBC cells, but we also constructed the HSA-Fe4 NPs delivery system. Structural analysis revealed that Fe4 binds within the IB subdomain of HSA, with His-146 coordinating the iron center. Importantly, Fe4/HSA-Fe4 NPs significantly suppressed the metastasis and growth of TNBC in vivo. Moreover, we elucidated the mechanisms by which Fe4/HSA-Fe4 NPs inhibited the growth and metastasis of TNBC: inducing Fenton reaction-mediated chemodynamic therapy, inducing ferroptosis, and tri-activating the immune response through the activation of the cGAS-STING pathway, the induction of immunogenic cell death, and the repolarization of M2 macrophages.

item.title: Discovery of Thiazolamide-based PI4KIIIβ/HDAC Dual Inhibitors with Potent Activity against Hepatitis C Virus
item.description:
Abstract
Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection remains a critical global public health burden affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide. The emergence of antiviral resistance persistently undermines the long-term clinical efficacy of current direct-acting antiviral (DAA) regimens, creating an urgent need for therapeutics with different mechanisms of action. Host-directed multi-target therapy offers a promising avenue to overcome DAA resistance, yet dual inhibitors targeting HCV-essential host kinase phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase IIIβ (PI4KIIIβ) and epigenetic regulator histone deacetylases (HDACs) have not been reported for HCV treatment to date. Herein, we describe the rational design, chemical synthesis, and comprehensive biological evaluation of a series of novel thiazolamide-based dual PI4KIIIβ/HDAC inhibitors. Lead compounds displayed potent dual-target enzymatic inhibition, robust in vitro anti-HCV activity and excellent in vivo tolerability. This work establishes a novel host-directed dual-target therapeutic paradigm for HCV, providing a viable strategy to address the unmet clinical challenge of DAA resistance.

item.title: Discovery of a Novel Dual Inhibitor Targeting Tubulin and Histone Deacetylase 8 for Treatment of the Ovarian Cancer
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, a series of novel dual inhibitors against both tubulin and histone deacetylase (HDAC) were designed and synthesized by integrating the natural product Millepachine with the key pharmacophore of HDAC inhibitors. Among them, compound 6 exhibited potent antiproliferative activity against 12 cancer cell lines, with IC50 values ranging from 0.020 to 0.244 μM. Mechanistic investigations revealed that compound 6 inhibited both tubulin polymerization (IC50 2.0 μM) and HDAC8 (IC50 0.110 μM), with 54-, 27- and 132-fold selectivity over HDAC1, HDAC4 and HDAC6, respectively. In an ovarian cancer xenograft mouse model, compound 6 exhibited significant inhibitory effect on tumor growth with a favorable safety profile. These findings identify compound 6 as a promising tubulin/HDAC8 dual inhibitor for further investigation.

item.title: Evaluation of 68 Ga Labeling Strategies and Thermostability of HER2-Targeted Nanobody NB46
item.description:
Abstract
The HER2-targeted nanobody NB46 was evaluated for labeling strategy flexibility and thermostability. Random and site-specific 68Ga labeling strategies were compared. Both conjugates exhibited high HER2 affinity, comparable to unmodified NB46. Cellular uptake, pharmacokinetics, micro-PET/CT imaging, and biodistribution in HER2-positive and HER2-negative tumor-bearing mice revealed no significant differences between the two strategies. NB46 retained HER2 affinity at temperatures up to 90 °C, demonstrating exceptional thermostability. Both conjugates achieved >95% radiochemical yields at all tested temperatures. Micro-PET/CT imaging showed sustained high tumor uptake with renal clearance as the primary elimination pathway. Blocking studies confirmed that NB46 and trastuzumab competitively bind to HER2. Elevated labeling temperatures did not compromise tumor targeting but resulted in a mild increase in renal uptake, notably for the random conjugate at 90 °C. These findings suggest that random labeling may represent a simpler, equally effective alternative for 68Ga-NB46 preparation, and confirm the excellent thermostability of this nanobody scaffold.

item.title: Design, Synthesis and Evaluation Donepezil-Based Dual BuChE/FAAH Inhibitors for Alzheimer’s Disease Therapy
item.description:
Abstract
Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is multifactorial, prompting multi-target therapy. A series of donepezil-based derivatives were designed, synthesized, and evaluated as dual inhibitors of human butyrylcholinesterase (hBuChE) and fatty acid amide hydrolase (hFAAH). Among them, lead G15 displayed potent and balanced inhibition with IC50 values of 2.44 μM and 0.17 μM, respectively, and favorable selectivity over carboxylesterases CES1/2 (SI 14.4 and 8.4). G15 not only acted as a time-dependent, mixed-type hFAAH inhibitor and a pseudo-irreversible hBuChE inhibitor, but also exhibited good drug-like properties, including high BBB permeability and oral bioavailability (108%). Moreover, G15 chelated Zn2+, protected PC12 cells from oxidative stress, and promoted microglial M1 → M2 polarization. In an Aβ1−42-induced mouse model, G15 significantly reversed cognitive deficits, outperforming donepezil. Therefore, G15 is poised for further development as a promising multi-target candidate for AD therapy.
